purpose: One fixed development candidate to reduce the observed run-environment and pressure-context bias, without changing pressure labels or player eligibility.
training_policy: Complete matches strictly before January 1 of the evaluation year; no current-year target updates and no same-match fitting.
scoring_pace: score_before / (legal_balls_before + 12), clipped to [0,6]; first ball has zero observed pace. The 12-ball denominator regularizes early-innings noise without using future scores.
chase_target_rate: chase_target / 120, clipped to [0,6] in second innings, zero in first innings
required_rate: runs_required / balls_remaining, clipped to [0,6] in second innings, zero in first innings; report tail clipping
other_transforms: innings_progress = legal_balls_before/120; wickets_fraction = wickets_before/10; recent_wickets_fraction = recent_wickets/10; hinge terms max(required_rate-knot,0)
basis: Intercept, fixed IPL/T20I x innings 1/2 x phases 01-06/07-15/16-20 group indicators, continuous features, and each group indicator times each continuous feature. No player identifiers, current outcomes or pressure label.
standardization: Weighted training mean and population SD for every nonintercept basis column; constant training columns are disabled. No evaluation statistics are used.
run_model: Weighted ridge least squares, predictions floored at zero; report floor rate
wicket_model: Weighted ridge logistic regression with an unpenalized intercept
objective: Sum of recency-weighted losses plus 0.5*ridge_penalty*sum(nonintercept coefficient^2); run loss is 0.5*squared error. Penalty is fixed, not fitted or equivalent to the old prior event count.
validation: Reuse baseline_validation_v1.json unchanged, including no material supported-group calibration alerts. Also require each target pooled primary loss no worse than the original default baseline. No automatic promotion of a partially passing candidate.
failure_policy: Keep both benchmarks and the failed gate. Do not test a second candidate, retune coefficients/penalties/thresholds or open reserved outcomes automatically.
limitations: Pre-ball pace can reflect earlier contributions by the same player; the result measures performance conditional on established innings state, not total player-created value. Historical recency cannot know future scoring conditions. Venue/opposition effects remain unmodeled. Development data already informed this amendment, so development improvements are not independent confirmation.
